objective: Produce compact, method- and mechanism-preserving Skin_Reaction auxiliary vocabularies without imposing a fixed vocabulary size.

namespace_policy.rule: Every semantic decision applies to exactly one source/output namespace. Similar labels in another namespace require a separate decision and may remain different.

preserve_when_explicit: in vivo, ex vivo, in vitro, or clinical setting
required_distinctions: llna versus llna-da versus gpmt versus buehler test versus hript
3t3 nru versus mtt versus reconstructed epidermis test

preserve_when_explicit: clinical sensitization versus individual AOP key event
required_distinctions: cysteine depletion versus lysine depletion versus gsh depletion
endpoint.allowed_equivalence: Cysteine depletion and cysteine peptide depletion may share one concept when no other measurement distinction is explicit.

species.default_form: Concise lowercase base species; deduplicate, alphabetize, and join multiple explicit species with ' + '.
forbidden_inference_sources: assay abbreviation except an explicitly licensed official expansion
species.phototoxicity_system_rule: The phototoxicity species/system namespace may retain explicit broad systems such as animal in vivo, in vitro cells, ex vivo tissue, reconstructed tissue, or non-biological/computational context.

merge.meaning: Map two or more equivalent labels to one label within one namespace.

rename.meaning: Replace one label without changing its raw-value scope.

split.meaning: Divide one heterogeneous provisional label using explicit raw-value assignments.
requirements: Every affected raw value is assigned exactly once.
Assignments are deterministic, exhaustive, and non-overlapping.
Every child label has raw support.
No child label infers information absent from the raw source.

publication_requires: Every non-null label has one primary disposition.
Every proposed change has a checker and adjudicator with identities distinct from the primary reviewer.
Every split has exact raw-value coverage.

forbidden_decisions: Any merge, rename, or split spanning multiple source/output namespaces.
Any decision involving a frozen passthrough namespace.
Any merge that erases an explicit protected method, model, mechanism, nucleophile, biomarker, setting, or species distinction.
Any species or method inferred from a cell line, reagent, abbreviation not licensed by the source contract, or outside knowledge.
Any vocabulary-size target used as the sole justification for a semantic merge.
Any unreviewed change to the runtime mapping.
